dimant-polarizednorms-choice.quote: In polarized environments, most individuals prefer extreme actions, which expose them to considerable strategic risk, to intermediate actions that minimize such risk.
dimant-polarizednorms-choice.version: Dimant, Gelfand, Hochleitner & Sonderegger, Management Science 71(3):2245-2263 (March 2025), published version, hosted by coauthor: https://www.michelegelfand.com/_files/ugd/6df109_20edd4d076c5479b8c7221bf8a8b7552.pdf [PDF page 1]
dimant-polarizednorms-choice.note: Abstract, verbatim. The only percentage the paper gives for this (Section 5.1, polarized treatment with a LOW mean) is: "Yet, we find that a sizeable share of our subjects (46%, of which 41% contribute four) does precisely that", i.e. 46% contributed MORE THAN TWO (exposing themselves to strategic risk), 41% of whom contributed the maximum four. The 46% is not a share choosing extremes and does not contradict "most"; the paper does not print a share of extreme choices pooled across polarized treatments. "Most chose extremes" is therefore the paper's own abstract claim, not a figure-level statistic.
